conditions.label: Sepsis due to Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus

documents.title: Discharge summary received; antibiotic course
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital discharge summary from the November admission arrived today and is filed. Called pt to confirm: last cefazolin dose at dialysis 12/22, no fevers since, fistula looks normal to him and the unit. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Summary reviewed: MSSA bacteremia, repeat cultures negative, TTE without vegetation, cefazolin finished 12/22. Problem resolved. Keep the February visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Recovered from the November infection; energy back to his usual. No fevers. Dialysis on schedule, fistula working well. Sugars fasting 110s-170s, no lows since the spring 2022 episode.

Exam: BP R arm as charted, afebrile. L AVF without redness, good thrill. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
T2DM - A1c and CBC today.
ESRD/anemia - per nephrology.
Lung screening: at 72 and 15 years from quitting this year, he is near the end of eligibility; he'd rather not do another scan. Respecting that.
RTC May.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Friday visit, between dialysis days was not possible this week. He's tired after this morning's treatment but otherwise well. No fevers, no breathing trouble, no lows. Taking meds as listed. Walks to the end of the road most days.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Alert, conversational. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. L AVF thrill. Feet: skin intact, sensation normal.

A/P
T2DM - A1c, lipids, CBC today. Glargine 24 qhs, lispro scale unchanged.
HTN - lisinopril 5.
ESRD on HD, anemia of CKD - nephrology.
History of TB - no symptoms.
Wellness visit and eye exam due this summer. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Results from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Washington - A1c 7.4, steady. Cholesterol fine on the atorvastatin. Blood count about where it usually runs on dialysis. Nothing to change. See you in August.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel his 8/22 wellness visit - ride service can't take him on a non-dialysis day this month and daughter is working. He'll call back to rebook in the fall. Offered video; he'd rather come in person.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting 90-day refills: insulin glargine pens, insulin lispro pens, pen needles, test strips, lisinopril 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin. Last office visit 5/24/2024. Sent per PCP with one refill each. Left message for pt: overdue for his visit, please call to schedule.

documents.title: Dialysis unit records
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Dialysis unit fax: influenza vaccine (high-dose) given in the unit 10/7/2024. December monthly labs attached. Filed.

documents.title: Time for a check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Washington, our records show we haven't seen you since last May. We'd like to get your yearly wellness visit and diabetes check on the calendar. We can do an early afternoon on a non-dialysis day, or a video visit. Reply here or call the front desk.

documents.title: Re: Time for a check-in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Daughter here. Dad is ok, just worn out with the 3 days a week of dialysis and the kidney doctor checks his blood every month. We'll try to get him in this summer. His shoulders have been bothering him, the kidney doctor is sending him to someone for that.

events.reason: bilateral shoulder pain and stiffness, hand numbness

reports.text: Bilateral shoulders, AP and axillary views. Subchondral bone cysts in both humeral heads with marginal erosions. Joint spaces preserved. No fracture or dislocation. No soft tissue calcification.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral subchondral cysts and erosions of the humeral heads.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice - new patient consultation, seen 05/13/2025. Referred by his nephrologist; copy to primary care.

HPI: 73-year-old man on long-term hemodialysis, with a staph access bloodstream infection in 2023 and anemia of CKD. For six months his shoulders have hurt and stiffened, increasingly so; he can no longer lift his arms above his head and has seen fullness around both shoulders. Both hands go numb and tingle, mostly at night.
PMH: ESRD on HD (L AVF); type 2 diabetes; hypertension; anemia of CKD; pulmonary TB, treated 2020-21; hypoglycemia 2022; pulmonary edema 2022; MSSA bacteremia 2023.
PSH: L AVF; R IJ dialysis catheter (removed); L carpal tunnel release.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u qhs, insulin lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker (40 pk-yr). No alcohol. Retired postal employee.

Exam: both shoulders enlarged with joint hypertrophy, tender on palpation; active and passive motion limited by pain. Reduced sensation over the median nerve territory of both hands.

Labs: creatinine 6.5, BUN 55, Hgb 10.2, Ca 9.2, phosphorus 5.0. Beta-2 microglobulin 34 mg/L (elevated).
Imaging: shoulder radiographs - subchondral bone cysts and erosions.

Impression: dialysis-related (beta-2 microglobulin) amyloidosis with shoulder arthropathy and bilateral median neuropathy at the wrist.
Plan:
- Acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tablets up to three times daily as needed; avoid NSAIDs.
- Physical therapy for shoulder range of motion.
- Letter to nephrology regarding dialysis adequacy/clearance.
- Follow-up as needed.

documents.title: Rheumatology note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: We received the rheumatology note from May. They think the shoulder and hand symptoms come from a protein that builds up with long-term dialysis, and suggested acetaminophen, physical therapy and coordination with his kidney team. I'd still like to see him in person to go over this and catch up on his diabetes - please call to book.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request for glargine, lispro, pen needles, strips, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Last seen 5/2024. PCP approved a 90-day supply. Called daughter - she'll try to book after the holidays; transport remains the issue.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request: insulin pens and needles, test strips, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Sent per PCP, 90 days. Note to pt via pharmacy: needs a visit for further refills - video is fine.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT head. Lateral and third ventricles enlarged out of proportion to the sulci. No cortical atrophy. No hemorrhage, mass or acute infarct. Basal cisterns patent.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology clinic - consultation, seen 05/18/2026. Copy to primary care (sent at family request).

HPI: 74-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, seen by rheumatology about a year ago for dialysis-related amyloidosis. Here with his daughter, who describes six months of worsening walking: his feet seem stuck to the floor, steps are short and shuffling, and getting started is hard. She has also noticed he forgets more and has had several episodes of urinary incontinence.
PMH: ESRD on HD; T2DM; HTN; anemia of CKD; treated pulmonary TB; prior hypoglycemia, pulmonary edema and MSSA access bacteremia; dialysis-related amyloidosis.
PSH: L AVF; R IJ catheter (removed); L carpal tunnel release.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u qhs, insulin lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, no alcohol. Daughter close by.

Exam: alert; oriented to person and place, not to date. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

CT head (today): enlarged ventricles without cortical atrophy.
Lumbar puncture today: opening pressure within normal limits; CSF analysis unremarkable.

Impression: normal pressure hydrocephalus (gait disturbance, cognitive change, urinary incontinence; ventriculomegaly).
Plan:
- High-volume tap test with timed gait before and after; our office will schedule.
- If gait improves, neurosurgery referral for shunt evaluation; we will arrange.
- Fall precautions at home; daughter to supervise walking outdoors.

documents.title: Neurology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Desmond's daughter. He saw a neurologist in May because his walking has gotten bad and he's more forgetful. They said fluid on the brain (normal pressure something) and want to do another spinal tap and maybe send him to a brain surgeon. Did you get their note? What should we be doing? He's still on dialysis M/W/F.

documents.title: Re: Neurology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. We didn't have the note, so we requested it this morning and it just came in. The neurologist diagnosed normal pressure hydrocephalus - extra fluid in the brain's ventricles that can affect walking, memory and bladder control. Their office is setting up a larger-volume spinal tap to see whether his walking improves, and if it does they will arrange a neurosurgery consult about a shunt. In the meantime please stay close when he walks outside and keep paths at home clear. I would really like to see him - it's been over two years. We can do a visit on a non-dialysis afternoon or a video visit to start. Please call the front desk to book.
